summary: Steel I-S fire tower, built 1934 per register (1935 newspaper says soon to be erected), removed 1962; the mountain now has a private Cold War concrete microwave tower.

facts.design: steel I-S tower (register); 80-foot forest fire tower (1935 Gettysburg Times item)
facts.status_note: Fire tower removed in 1962 per the register; a separate Cold War concrete microwave tower (Cannonball) on the mountain is on private property, and no source describes remains of the fire tower
facts.agency: Pennsylvania department of forests (per the 1935 Gettysburg Times item)

access.note: Applies to the Cannonball concrete tower atop Cross Mountain, on private property and not accessible to the public; no access information for the 1934 fire-tower site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register gives 1934 as the build year; the March 5, 1935 Gettysburg Times item, as quoted by Forest Lookouts, says the 80-foot tower will soon be erected. The story says the sources disagree on the year and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: The build year is disputed (1934 register vs 1935 newspaper). The brief's coordinates (39.72843, -77.99167) are essentially the same point as the Cannonball map pin in a Virtual Globetrotting page (mytopo link 39.7283, -77.99160), so they may mark the concrete microwave tower, not the 1934 fire tower; verify before using them. The Cannonball description comes from a visit made by special permission, and the page gives no visit date. Do not encourage visits: the concrete tower is on private property.
